hardDay.heading: Hard day? Start here.
hardDay.body:
Finishing a book doesn't mean you've arrived. The Christian life doesn't graduate into a finished map. If this week is heavy, your task is honesty and one trusted believer.

Come to Jesus tired. He gives rest. Read "Guardrails One Last Time" when you can.

If you are in danger, or you are having thoughts of not wanting to live, please stop here and reach out now. In the U.S., call or text 988, or call 911. Then tell a pastor or a trusted believer today.

read.heading: Read first: the Conclusion
read.body:
Open to the Conclusion, "A Life in Motion." Read "A Pastoral Charge" and "Live a Life in Motion." If you can, read "Where We've Walked" too.

You'll see the whole road. Part 1, what faith really is. Part 2, the engine: purpose, the Spirit, wisdom. Part 3, the barriers: fear, fog, and what's in your hand.

And you'll see the chair again. I come back to where I started, and to what I had to learn the hard way about trust. Read it slowly. Then come back and we'll write your Rule of Motion.

bookRef.section: A Pastoral Charge; Live a Life in Motion

prompts: What sentence in the Conclusion landed hardest?

pulse.heading: The pulse: faith rests, and faith moves
pulse.body:
Faith rests in God and moves in obedience. You don't have to choose between trust and purpose.

Grace doesn't cancel purpose. Grace launches it. That's where we started at Stop 0, and it's where we land.
pulse.quote: You do not have to choose between trusting God and living on purpose.
prompts: After this book, what is my Great Christian Standstill in one honest sentence?

nameIt.heading: Name it: which guardrail?
nameIt.body:
The Conclusion holds the guardrails one last time. This isn't hustle religion. It isn't passive "trust." And holy waiting is still real.

You probably lean one way. Be honest about which guardrail you need most, so faith in motion doesn't become either a whip or a permission slip.
prompts: Which guardrail do I need more: against hustle, or against passive "trust"?
Compare my standstill sentence from Stop 0 with today's. What changed?
What will "trust as a child, steward as a servant, walk on" look like on Monday morning?

build.heading: Build it: My Rule of Motion
build.body:
The Pastoral Charge gives four moves: name the fear, take the clear next duty, use what's in your hand, and walk in the fog with lamp-light.

Turn those into your Rule of Motion. Not a manifesto you admire. A few plain lines you can actually live. Keep each one short enough to remember on a hard Tuesday.
prompts: When fear shows up in church clothes, I will:
When the next duty is clear, I will:
With what's in my hand, I will:
When it's foggy, I will:
The person who will hold me to this:

move.heading: Move: this week's practice
move.body:
From the end of the Conclusion:

One fear named, one duty taken, one gift used, all in the same week. No stadium lights required.

That's it. Three things, one week. If you miss, set a new date within three days and keep walking.
prompts: One fear named
One duty taken
One gift used
Missed one? New date (within three days):
move.cta: Close the app and go take your step

help.heading: Help: invite someone to walk with you
help.body:
Bring your Rule of Motion to a trusted believer this week and read it to them.

Then think about who could walk these stops next. Faith in motion spreads one person at a time, one friend walking with another. Invite one friend to take one step a week with you. Or give them a copy of the book.
prompts: Who I'll read my Rule of Motion to:
One friend I'll invite to walk with me (first name or initials):
help.cta: Send it, then put the phone down

pray.heading: Pray it: rest and walk
pray.body:
Come to Him tired, and walk on rested.

Jesus, thank You for grace that saved me and grace that sends me. I'm not choosing between trusting You and living on purpose. I'm doing both, with Your help.

Keep me from hustle and from hiding. Here is my Rule of Motion: ____.

Teach me to trust as a child, steward as a servant, and walk on. Amen.

verses.text: Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”

prompts: My Rule of Motion, in one line:

review.heading: Review: walk on
review.body:
After this week, mark it: took the steps, not yet, or holy wait.

You've walked all twelve stops. That's not a finish line. Faith doesn't graduate into a finished map. Keep coming back on Sundays to review your week. And when you're ready, start again with a new focus.

If something changed in your life when you took your step, I'd be honored to hear it. Tap "Share what changed."
review.quote: Trust as a child. Steward as a servant. Walk on.
prompts: How did it go? I took the steps / Not yet, and I can name the block / Holy wait, and I can say why
What happened:
The step I'm taking next:
review.cta: Close the app and walk on
